s0201.literal: Though one may all day hand on sword, all night beat the watch, glare to struggle over gain and loss, and work up breath to seek victory and defeat—in whom does it rest?
s0201.idiomatic: Though one may clutch a sword all day and beat the night watch, glare to fight over gain and loss, and work up breath to win or lose—in whom does it finally rest?

s0202.literal: Minded and unminded—they merely wish to distinguish empty space.
s0202.idiomatic: Minded versus unminded—they only try to carve distinctions in empty space.

s0203.literal: Why the intent not to allow me to discourse but to make me yield and withdraw?
s0203.idiomatic: Why refuse to let me argue and instead make me yield and withdraw?

s0206.literal: [imperial edict] has already soared into the vast sky, [5] yet the lookout still peeks into marshes seeking it.
s0206.idiomatic: [The imperial edict] has already soared into the vast sky, [5] yet the apprehensive still peek into marshes seeking it.

s0208.literal: A true man ought to spread this Way.
s0208.idiomatic: A true man ought to spread this Way.

s0209.literal: The Non-Contention Treatise says: the way of non-contention penetrates within and without.
s0209.idiomatic: The Non-Contention Treatise says: the way of non-contention runs through inner and outer alike.

s0210.literal: What you say must be contended—this uses the branch to save the root and loses the root while tending the branch.
s0210.idiomatic: When you say one must contend, that uses the branch to save the root and loses the root while tending the branch.

s0211.literal: Now I will speak to you on it.
s0211.idiomatic: Now I will explain it to you.

s0213.literal: If one follows external classics and seeks before written contracts, in the utmost pure age hearts were plain and simple and the teaching of wordlessness was practiced—at that time the people to old age did not visit one another, yet each obtained his place; what contention was there again?
s0213.idiomatic: If one follows secular classics back before written records, in the most pristine age hearts were plain and the wordless teaching held sway—then people lived to old age without visiting one another, yet each had his place; what contention could there be?

s0216.literal: [end] does not contend, [6] which is the truth of things.
s0216.idiomatic: [The end] does not contend, [6] which is the truth of things.

s0217.literal: He replied: contention and non-contention cannot be one-sidedly clung to.
s0217.idiomatic: He replied: contention and non-contention cannot be clung to one-sidedly.

s0218.literal: Root and branch—how again can one know?
s0218.idiomatic: Root and branch—how can one know for certain?

s0219.literal: From of old not contending—how does one know it is not the branch?
s0219.idiomatic: If from of old there is no contention, how do you know that is not the branch?

s0220.literal: Contending today—what proof that it is not the root?
s0220.idiomatic: If one contends today, what proof that it is not the root?

s0221.literal: Standing behind and looking forward, then it is forward;
s0221.idiomatic: Standing behind and looking forward, that is forward;

s0222.literal: standing in front and looking back, then it is back.
s0222.idiomatic: standing in front and looking back, that is behind.

s0223.literal: Yet matters of before and after are still like this and that—that calls this "that," this calls that "that"; the name of this and that—who truly occupies the place?
s0223.idiomatic: Yet before and after are like this and that—each side calls the other "that"; the names this and that—who really holds the place?

s0224.literal: Spoken thus, the myriad affairs can be known.
s0224.idiomatic: Put this way, the myriad affairs become knowable.

s0225.literal: Root and branch, before and after, right and wrong, good and evil—can they be eternally held?
s0225.idiomatic: Root and branch, before and after, right and wrong, good and evil—can any of them be held forever?

s0226.literal: How can one trust one's own cleverness and discard others' ears and eyes?
s0226.idiomatic: How can one trust one's own cleverness and discard others' ears and eyes?

s0227.literal: Water bubbles arise and perish, the fire-wheel turns—entering the pit trap, receiving fetters, giving birth to worry and fear, raising vexations—what is the loss?
s0227.idiomatic: Water bubbles rise and burst, the fire-wheel spins—one enters the pit, wears fetters, breeds worry and fear, and raises vexations—what is lost?

s0228.literal: Not corresponding to the Way and therefore raising the various views—that is why.
s0228.idiomatic: It is because one fails to correspond to the Way and instead raises fixed views.

s0229.literal: Those who correspond are not so—there is non-action, and there is nothing not done.
s0229.idiomatic: Those who correspond are otherwise—there is non-action, and there is nothing left undone.

s0230.literal: Good and evil cannot go together, yet one has never left good and evil; birth and death cannot arrive, yet one is ultimately still in birth and death—therefore one can forever leave and let go.
s0230.idiomatic: Good and evil cannot coincide, yet one never leaves them; birth and death cannot be reached, yet one remains in them—therefore one can forever leave and let go.

s0231.literal: Therefore the sage, mindful that winding bonds are not shed and pitying how sticky glue is hard to leave, earnestly teaches and shows, providing every expedient.
s0231.idiomatic: Therefore the sage, seeing that winding bonds are not shed and pitying how sticky glue is hard to leave, earnestly teaches and provides every expedient.

s0232.literal: Those who hope for the goal, crossing and seeking, have their kinds; though unicorn horns are hard to complete and images are easy to lose, how can one not take the distant road as model and urge on the short morning?
s0232.idiomatic: Seekers on the path still have their kind; though a unicorn's horn is hard to finish and likenesses slip away, how can one not take the far road as model and press on through the brief dawn?

s0233.literal: One should only reflect on good and evil in one's own person, not measure other things and wish to distinguish, saying "I am clever, my insight, my reckoning, my thinking"—spoken thus, it is also crude.
s0233.idiomatic: One should reflect on the good and evil in oneself, not measure other things and try to divide them up, saying "I am clever, I see, I reckon, I think"—that too is crude.

s0234.literal: Other people are truly hard to measure; they may indeed be ordinary men as they seem, or they may be sages bending to match what custom at the time should see and what karmic retribution should display.
s0234.idiomatic: Others are truly hard to fathom; they may be ordinary men as they seem, or sages stooping to what the times should see and what karmic retribution should show.

s0235.literal: How can one give free rein to the breast, exhaust nature and disposition, and then breed ridicule?
s0235.idiomatic: How can one give free rein to the breast, exhaust one's nature, and then breed ridicule?

s0236.literal: One should only empty oneself and wander in the world, bowing and looking up in the space between lightning and dew.
s0236.idiomatic: One should empty oneself and wander the world, bowing and rising in the span between lightning and dew.

s0237.literal: The bright moon is in the sky—all waters alike see it; the clear wind reaches the grove—all pipes together sound.
s0237.idiomatic: The bright moon is in the sky and every water reflects it; the clear wind reaches the grove and every pipe sounds.

s0238.literal: How would I go against things?
s0238.idiomatic: How would I go against things?

s0239.literal: Not entering among salted fish, not sweet on rotten rats.
s0239.idiomatic: Not entering among salted fish, not sweet on rotten rats.

s0240.literal: How would I be the same as things?
s0240.idiomatic: How would I be the same as things?

s0241.literal: Who can know me and walk this road together?
s0241.idiomatic: Who can know me and walk this road with me?

s0244.literal: How again can one see contention as wrong and non-contention as right?
s0244.idiomatic: How again can one treat contention as wrong and non-contention as right?

s0245.literal: Then those who contend contend of themselves, and those who do not contend do not contend of themselves—I take both and use them.
s0245.idiomatic: Let those who contend contend on their own and those who do not contend refrain on their own—I take both and use them.

s0246.literal: Better that the Dharma master not waste effort, dotting brush and paper, but only declare non-contention;
s0246.idiomatic: Better that the Dharma master spare the effort of dotting brush and paper and only preach non-contention;

s0247.literal: the disciple wear out lips and tongue, consume the sundial's drip—only facing the illumined Way?
s0247.idiomatic: while the disciple wear out lips and tongue and consume the sundial's drip—only to face the illumined Way?

s0250.literal: If one must for the moment examine truth and falsehood and briefly observe gain and loss, nothing surpasses relying on the words of sages and worthies, checking conduct and hiding, studying beginning and end, collating inner and outer, so that floating phrases have no use and deceitful ways naturally vanish.
s0250.idiomatic: If one must for the moment test truth and falsehood and briefly weigh gain and loss, nothing surpasses relying on sages and worthies, checking conduct and intent, studying beginning and end, collating inner and outer, so floating phrases fail and deceitful ways vanish of themselves.

s0251.literal: Please wait for the later session and observe its subtlety.
s0251.idiomatic: Please wait for the later session and observe its subtlety.

s0252.literal: Soon thereafter, in his original office he was concurrently made unranked gentleman attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry on mission to Qi; on return he was made gentleman attendant of the scattered cavalry and adviser to the Prince of Shixing, General Who Pacifies the South, concurrently eastern palace recorder.
s0252.idiomatic: Soon, retaining his original post, he was also made unranked gentleman attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry on mission to Qi; on his return he was made gentleman attendant of the scattered cavalry and adviser to the Prince of Shixing, general who pacifies the south, while retaining his eastern palace recorder post.

s0253.literal: He passed through crown prince household supervisor and steward, still concurrently recorder as before.
s0253.idiomatic: He served as crown prince household supervisor and steward, still keeping the recorder post.

s0254.literal: When Houzhu took the throne he was moved to director of the secretariat and right guard general, concurrently secretariat attendant for current affairs, in charge of edicts and letters.
s0254.idiomatic: When Houzhu took the throne he was made director of the secretariat and right guard general, concurrently secretariat attendant for current affairs, in charge of edicts.

s0255.literal: Zai's writing was classical and ornate; his nature was also quick and sharp—even on great affairs of army and state, when he put brush to paper it was at once complete; he never drafted beforehand, and even those who pondered deeply could not surpass him; Houzhu valued him greatly.
s0255.idiomatic: Zai wrote in a classical, ornate style and was quick by nature—even on great military and state affairs his brush finished at once; he never drafted beforehand, and even deep thinkers could not surpass him; Houzhu valued him greatly.

s0256.literal: Yet his nature was wooden and strong; he did not hold to restraint and conduct, relied on talent and gave rein to temper, and insulted people—court gentlemen mostly harbored resentment.
s0256.idiomatic: Yet he was stiff by nature, held to no restraint, relied on talent and vented his temper, and insulted others—most court gentlemen resented him.

s0257.literal: It happened that Shi Wenqing and Shen Keqing through fawning and favoritism were close and cherished, monopolizing the balance of power, while Zai grew still more distant.
s0257.idiomatic: Shi Wenqing and Shen Keqing won favor through flattery, monopolized power, and Zai grew still more distant.

s0258.literal: Wenqing and the others therefore together slandered Zai for receiving gold from a Goguryeo envoy; Houzhu arrested Zai and put him in prison.
s0258.idiomatic: Wenqing and the others then slandered Zai for taking gold from a Goguryeo envoy; Houzhu had him arrested and imprisoned.

s0259.literal: Zai by nature was firm; in indignant rage he thereupon submitted a memorial from prison, saying: "The ruler ought to respectfully serve the Supreme Lord, love and cherish the people below, reduce cravings and desires, keep far from flattery and favoritism, at unclear dawn seek clothing, at sundown forget food—thereby grace covers the realm and blessing flows to sons and grandsons.
s0259.idiomatic: Zai was by nature unyielding; in rage he submitted a memorial from prison: "A ruler should respectfully serve Heaven, love the people, curb desire, keep far from flatterers, rise at unclear dawn and forget food at sundown—then grace covers the realm and blessing reaches his heirs.

s0260.literal: Your Majesty of late has passed bounds in wine and sex, is not reverent toward the spirits of the suburban altars, and dotes on the ghosts of lewd darkness alone;
s0260.idiomatic: Your Majesty of late has gone to excess in wine and sex, neglects the spirits of the suburban altars, and dotes only on ghosts of lewd darkness;

s0261.literal: petty men are at your side, palace eunuchs toy with power, you hate the loyal and straight as enemies, and regard living people as grass and stubble;
s0261.idiomatic: petty men stand at your side, eunuchs toy with power, you hate the loyal and upright as enemies, and treat the people like grass;

s0262.literal: in the rear palace trailing brocade and embroidery, in the stables horses leave grain and millet surplus, while the people wander displaced and stiff corpses cover the wilds;
s0262.idiomatic: the rear palace trails brocade while stable horses leave grain unused, the people wander homeless, and stiff corpses cover the wilds;

s0263.literal: bribes go openly, the treasury is drained, the spirits are angry and the people resentful, the masses rebel and kin turn away.
s0263.idiomatic: bribes run openly, the treasury drains, spirits rage and the people resent, the masses rebel and kin turn away.

s0264.literal: I fear the kingly qi of the southeast ends from this.
s0264.idiomatic: I fear the kingly qi of the southeast ends here.

s0265.literal: " When the memorial was submitted Houzhu was greatly enraged.
s0265.idiomatic: " When the memorial arrived Houzhu was furious.

s0266.literal: Before long his mind eased somewhat; he sent an envoy to tell Zai: "I wish to pardon you—can you reform your faults?
s0266.idiomatic: Before long his anger cooled somewhat; he sent an envoy to tell Zai, "I wish to pardon you—can you reform your faults?

s0267.literal: " Zai replied: "My mind is like my face; if my face can change, then my mind can change.
s0267.idiomatic: " Zai replied, "My mind is like my face; if my face can change, then my mind can change.

s0268.literal: " Houzhu thereupon grew still more angry and ordered the eunuch Li Shanqing to investigate the matter to the end, [7] and Zai was granted death in prison, aged fifty-five.
s0268.idiomatic: " Houzhu then grew still angrier and ordered the eunuch Li Shanqing to investigate to the end, [7] and Zai was ordered to die in prison, aged fifty-five.

s0269.literal: He had a collected works in ten scrolls circulating in the world.
s0269.idiomatic: A collected works in ten scrolls circulated after his death.

s0270.literal: At the time there was Zhang Hua of Wuxing, styled Zhongzong; his family for generations were farmers—to Hua alone he loved learning, associated with gentlemen and scholars, and broadly read the classics and histories, skilled at composition.
s0270.idiomatic: At the time Zhang Hua of Wuxing, styled Zhongzong, came from a farming family—he alone loved learning, kept company with scholars, read widely in the classics and histories, and wrote well.

s0271.literal: In the turmoil of Hou Jing he then traveled to Lingnan, lived at Luofu Mountain Temple, and devoted himself to study.
s0271.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's turmoil he fled to Lingnan, lived at Luofu Mountain Temple, and devoted himself to study.

s0272.literal: Ouyang Fu was inspector of Guangzhou and appointed him Administrator of Nanhai.
s0272.idiomatic: Ouyang Fu, inspector of Guangzhou, appointed him administrator of Nanhai.

s0273.literal: When Ouyang He was defeated he then returned to the capital.
s0273.idiomatic: When Ouyang He was defeated he returned to the capital.

s0274.literal: In the Taichu era Emperor Gaozong sent Vice Minister of Personnel Xiao Yin to instruct Guangzhou Inspector Ma Jing to send his son in as hostage; Yin memorialized that Hua should go with him on the mission.
s0274.idiomatic: In the Taichu era Emperor Gaozong sent Vice Minister of Personnel Xiao Yin to instruct Guangzhou inspector Ma Jing to send his son as hostage; Yin memorialized that Hua should accompany the mission.

s0275.literal: When the mission returned, Emperor Gaozong had died.
s0275.idiomatic: When the mission returned, Emperor Gaozong had died.

s0276.literal: When Houzhu took the throne the court gentlemen, because Hua by nature had no meritorious background, all competed to slander him; he was therefore made director of the great market. As it was utterly not to his liking, he pleaded illness and resigned, depressed and without achieving his aim.
s0276.idiomatic: When Houzhu took the throne, court gentlemen—Hua had no record of merit—competed to slander him; he was made director of the great market. That post ill suited him; he pleaded illness and resigned, depressed and thwarted.

s0277.literal: Early in Zhenming he submitted a memorial of extreme remonstrance; its general purport said: "In the past the Founder southward pacified the Hundred Yue and northward punished the rebellious captive;
s0277.idiomatic: Early in Zhenming he submitted a memorial of fierce remonstrance, saying in gist: "In the past the Founder southward pacified the Hundred Yue and northward punished the rebel lord;

s0278.literal: Emperor Shizu eastward settled Wu and Kuaiji and westward broke Wang Lin;
s0278.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu eastward settled Wu and Kuaiji and westward broke Wang Lin;

s0279.literal: Emperor Gaozong recovered Huainan and opened land for a thousand li—the merit of the three ancestors was also utmost diligence.
s0279.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong recovered Huainan and opened land for a thousand li—the merit of the three ancestors was utmost diligence.

s0280.literal: Your Majesty has reigned now five years, not thinking of the former emperor's hardships, not knowing that Heaven's mandate is to be feared, drowning in favorites, deluded by wine and sex, sacrificing at the seven temples yet not going out, bowing to consorts yet holding court, old ministers and veteran generals cast to the wild grass, flatterers and slanderous villains raised into the court.
s0280.idiomatic: Your Majesty has reigned five years without remembering the former emperor's hardships or fearing Heaven's mandate, drowning in favorites and delusion of wine and sex, sacrificing at the seven temples yet not going out, bowing to consorts yet holding court, casting old ministers and veteran generals to the wilds and raising flatterers and slanderers.

s0281.literal: Now the frontier daily narrows and Sui troops press the border—if Your Majesty does not change the string and ease the bow, I see deer again roaming the Gusu Terrace.
s0281.idiomatic: Now the frontier shrinks daily and Sui troops press the border—if Your Majesty does not change course, I see deer roaming the Gusu Terrace again.

s0282.literal: " When the memorial was submitted Houzhu was greatly enraged and that same day ordered him beheaded.
s0282.idiomatic: " When the memorial arrived Houzhu was furious and ordered him beheaded that same day.

s0283.literal: The historiographer says: Xiao Ji and Lu Qiong both for talent and learning were illustrious; Gu Yewang's learning exhausted the canon; Fu Zai was sharp-witted and outstanding—all spirits of an age.
s0283.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Xiao Ji and Lu Qiong both shone for talent and learning; Gu Yewang mastered the canon; Fu Zai was brilliantly sharp—all spirits of an age.

s0284.literal: Yet Zai could not follow the Way in advancing and withdrawing and therefore fell into the utmost net—pitiable!
s0284.idiomatic: Yet Zai could not advance and withdraw by the Way and so fell into the utmost net—pitiable!

s0286.literal: Director of Revenue Wang Chang—the character chang was originally an ink dot in the base text and is restored from other editions.
s0286.idiomatic: On "Director of Revenue Wang Chang": chang was an ink dot in the base text and is restored from other editions.

s0289.literal: [Cheng] prince as inspector of Yang Province—changed according to the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions.
s0289.idiomatic: On "[Cheng] prince as inspector of Yang Province": emended per the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions.

s0290.literal: Received the Three Treatises from the Dharma master Huilang of Xinghuang—below "Xinghuang" the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions have the character si [temple].
s0290.idiomatic: On "received the Three Treatises from the Dharma master Huilang of Xinghuang": below Xinghuang, the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions add si (temple).

s0292.literal: [Jian] riding Jueyu—changed according to the Hall edition.
s0292.idiomatic: On "[Jian] riding Jueyu": emended per the Hall edition.

s0293.literal: Note: Wenyuan yinghua 747 also reads jian.
s0293.idiomatic: Note: Wenyuan yinghua 747 also reads jian.

s0296.literal: [imperial edict] has already soared into the vast sky—Zhang Senkai
s0296.idiomatic: On "[imperial edict] has already soared into the vast sky": Zhang Senkai

s0298.idiomatic: says peng ought to read imperial edict.

s0299.literal: Note: Jiaoming is a bird name; later the bird radical was added; Zhang's statement is correct; now changed accordingly.
s0299.idiomatic: Note: Jiaoming is a bird name; later the bird radical was added; Zhang is correct; the text is now emended accordingly.
